title: Microsoft Copilot Chat in Outlook: reasoning over inbox, calendar and enterprise data (Worldwide)
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, licensing, data boundaries and documented controls are supported. Minor corrections should complete the DLP route, cite the simulation guidance and acknowledge checklist controls missing from the table.

claims.quote:
Select Settings, then select Integrated Apps. Select the Available Apps list. Next, select the app you want to edit.
select the Users tab in the overview pane.

claims.claim: No API operation for the Copilot app's Integrated Apps self-install availability is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Microsoft Graph Exchange PowerShell integrated apps Copilot app block availability users API' and 'Copilot Integrated Apps API availability block'; read Integrated Apps, Manage Copilot Chat and copilotPackage:block. No matching self-install operation was documented.

claims.claim: The organisation-wide app block is in Microsoft 365 admin center at Settings > Integrated Apps > Available Apps > app > Block app.
claims.quote:
Select Settings, and then select Integrated Apps.
Select the Available Apps list.
Select an app from the Available Apps list to open the overview pane.
Select Block app.

claims.claim: No API equivalent for blocking the Copilot app through Integrated Apps is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Microsoft Graph Exchange PowerShell integrated apps Copilot app block availability users API' and 'Copilot Integrated Apps API availability block'; read Manage Copilot Chat, Integrated Apps and copilotPackage:block. The package API does not identify the Copilot app as its target.

claims.claim: Integrated Apps settings for the Copilot app apply to both Microsoft Copilot and Copilot Chat apps.
claims.quote: On the Integrated Apps page, the CoPilot app settings apply to both Microsoft Copilot and the Copilot Chat apps. Any changes made to this app from the integrated apps portal apply to both.

claims.claim: The availability setting governs self-installation and does not change admin-deployed apps.
claims.quote: The availability setting of an app doesn't impact any admin deployed apps. The availability setting only allows you to control which end users can install and use these apps on their own.

claims.claim: The Copilot app provides Copilot Chat in Outlook across web, desktop and mobile.
claims.quote: The Copilot app is an integrated app that provides Copilot Chat via web, in the Microsoft Copilot app (web, desktop, mobile) and in Outlook (web, desktop, mobile).

claims.claim: Microsoft advises preventing unlicensed users' app access by not deploying it to them and limiting self-install to a licensed-user group.
claims.quote:
To prevent access to the Copilot app for unlicensed users, including US government customers, don't deploy the Copilot app to these users.
select Specific users/group in the organization can install and assign a group that includes only licensed users.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Block app blocks the Copilot app tenant-wide, including users assigned a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence.
claims.quote: If you block the Copilot app using the Integrated app control, you block the Copilot app tenant-wide across the Microsoft Copilot app, Outlook, and the web, including for users assigned a Microsoft 365 Copilot license.

claims.claim: Turning off Let users access Microsoft apps in your tenant does not turn off the Copilot app.
claims.quote: Turning off the Let users access Microsoft apps in your tenant setting in Integrated Apps won't turn off the Copilot app.

claims.claim: The printed Purview route reaches the sensitivity-label condition for a custom Copilot DLP policy.
claims.quote:
Go to Data Loss Prevention > Policies and select + Create policy.
Select the Custom template, then Custom policy.
On the Locations page, set the Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork location to on.
Content contains > Sensitivity labels
claims.fix: The route stops at the condition rather than the enforcement action. Set controls[2].ui.path and its rendered counterpart to 'Data Loss Prevention > Policies > Create policy > Custom > Custom policy > Locations > Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork > Add a rule > Content contains > Sensitivity labels > Prevent Copilot and Cowork from processing content', using the setup steps and supported-actions table at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/dlp-microsoft365-copilot-location-learn-about.

claims.claim: New-DLPComplianceRule with -Name, -Policy, -AdvancedRule and -RestrictAccess containing ExcludeContentProcessing=Block creates the documented Copilot content-exclusion rule.
claims.quote: New-DLPComplianceRule -Name "Copilot Rule" -Policy "Copilot Policy" -AdvancedRule $advrule -RestrictAccess @(@{setting="ExcludeContentProcessing";value="Block"})

claims.claim: The sensitivity-label rule's enforcement action is Prevent Copilot and Cowork from processing content.
claims.quote: Content contains > Sensitivity labels | Prevent Copilot and Cowork from processing content

claims.where: controls[2]; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Sensitivity-label rules in the Copilot DLP location can prevent Copilot Chat from using labelled files and emails in responses.
claims.quote: Restrict Microsoft 365 Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Cowork from processing sensitive files and emails. You can create a DLP policy to prevent these Copilot experiences from using files and emails that have sensitivity labels when generating responses.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rendered table
claims.claim: Sensitivity-label email coverage is for emails sent on or after January 1, 2025.
claims.quote:
A rule configured to protect items with sensitivity labels applies to Microsoft 365 Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Cowork and supports the following content:
Emails sent on or after January 1, 2025.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Risk assessment; Governance guidance: At rollout; rendered table
claims.claim: Calendar invites are not supported by the sensitivity-label content restriction.
claims.quote: Calendar invites aren't supported.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: External email can ground Outlook Copilot Chat answers, and the external-email DLP restriction applies to these reasoning experiences in preview.
claims.quote: This feature is in preview. It applies to Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat, including email summarization and reasoning experiences that use email data.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The Copilot DLP location offers the condition Email is received from > External users to exclude external email.
claims.quote: create DLP policies that use the Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork policy location with the Email is received from > External users condition.

claims.claim: The external-email rule's action is Prevent Copilot from processing content.
claims.quote: The action is configured to Prevent Copilot from processing content.

claims.claim: Microsoft says excluding external email helps reduce prompt-injection and untrusted-data influence risks.
claims.quote: This protection helps organizations reduce the risk of prompt injection and untrusted data influence.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Prompts run in the initiating user's security context, requiring that user's existing content permissions.
claims.quote: All Microsoft 365 Copilot prompts run in the security context of the user who initiates the prompt. This means for a user to see an item in a prompt response, they must first have the necessary permissions to access the content of the item.

claims.claim: Copilot DLP policy scope follows the prompt submitter, not the email owner.
claims.quote: DLP policy scoping for Microsoft 365 Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Cowork is based on the user who submits the prompt, not the owner of a file or email that the experience accesses.

claims.claim: DLP changes can take up to four hours to reach the Copilot experiences.
claims.quote: Updates to a DLP policy can take up to four hours to reflect in the Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork experiences.

claims.claim: A DLP policy can start in simulation mode before enforcement.
claims.quote: Run the policy in simulation mode, otherwise known as simulation mode, for Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policies replaces the Test and Test with policy tips policy states.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/dlp-simulation-mode-learn to sources for the simulation-mode advice; the cited Copilot-specific page expressly names simulation for Microsoft 365 Copilot and Cowork, whereas this general DLP page states the policy-level mechanism.

claims.claim: The high-impact rationale describes the expansion as changing answers for every Copilot Chat user without a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence.
claims.quote: Copilot Chat in Outlook for affected users will expand from reasoning over a single email thread to reasoning over the user's entire inbox, calendar, meetings, and other enterprise data that is already available to them through Microsoft 365.
claims.fix: Keep impact high, but replace the rationale with 'High. It changes what Copilot Chat in Outlook answers from for affected Copilot Chat users without a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence, on desktop, web and mobile.' This retains the source's affected-user qualification rather than suggesting universal access regardless of app availability and prerequisites.
